page.title: Programs
page.purpose: The corpus of everything that has been submitted, grouped so a reader can ask which agent, which session, and which failure shape without leaving the list.

priorities.statement: Failures are findable without a query.
priorities.notes: The corpus exists to be read after something went wrong. A list that surfaces successes first optimizes for the case nobody opens it for.

priorities.statement: Agent-submitted and operator-submitted programs are visibly separate populations.
priorities.notes: Grouping by provenance is not cosmetic. Corpus mining excludes operator programs by default, and the list should make that exclusion legible rather than hidden in a query parameter.

priorities.statement: Grouping by agent and session is one interaction, not a report.
priorities.notes: 'This agent fails argument validation more than average' should be readable off a grouped list. Anything beyond that is agent-manager's job.

priorities.statement: The list never mounts the code editor.
priorities.notes: Snippets render with shiki. Monaco loads only when a program is opened, so the corpus stays fast at any size.

states.description: Programs are listed newest first with outcome, provenance, and session.
No program has ever been submitted; the page explains what a program is and how one arrives.
A filter or grouping is narrowing the corpus.
Some program records are missing detail — typically an interrupted session — and are marked rather than hidden.
The corpus could not be read and the reason is visible.

elements.name: Programs
elements.description: One row per submission: time, outcome, failure class, provenance, agent, session, materialization ratio.

elements.name: Outcome
elements.description: Succeeded, refused, invalid, or errored — the same four classes the program page uses.

elements.name: Submitted by
elements.description: Agent, operator, or both. Defaults to agent, matching the default corpus-mining population.

elements.name: Program preview
elements.description: Static highlighted snippet. Never a mounted editor.

elements.name: What a program is
elements.description: The teaching surface for a human arriving before any agent has run anything.

claims.statement: The page exposes a named corpus region containing the program list.
Provenance is shown per row and the active provenance filter is stated, not implied.
claims.rationale: OT-P1-008. A default filter that silently hides operator programs would make the corpus look smaller than it is; one that silently includes them would corrupt the mining population.

claims.statement: Grouping by agent shows outcome distribution per agent without navigating away.
claims.rationale: This is the closest thing to friction this console offers, and it is deliberately descriptive. The explanation lives in agent-manager.

claims.statement: With no programs submitted, the page explains what a program is and how one gets here.
claims.rationale: The primary user is an agent, so a human arriving cold has never used the product. Empty state is the only place they can learn it from this console.

claims.statement: Row previews render as static highlighted source; the code editor is not mounted on this page.
claims.rationale: Stated in docs/concepts/UI-ARCHITECTURE.md. Mounting Monaco per row makes the corpus unusable at scale for no gain.

claims.statement: A program whose record is incomplete is listed and marked rather than omitted.
claims.rationale: A silently dropped row makes the corpus look cleaner than it is, which is the failure mode the honesty contract exists to prevent.

claims.statement: Loading, empty, searching, partial, and error states each render dedicated content.
The filter, the grouping control, and every program row are reachable by keyboard alone.
